title: European tour of 1952: Denmark, Paris, England
summary: She describes crowds at Albert Hall, Paris and Denmark and a six-week stay in Europe.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You have traveled a great deal, Miami, haven't you? Yes, I've traveled all over.

I've been everywhere in the United States. And of course, I was in Europe, your part of the country, uh, in 52. Yeah? And I was so well received there. I've sold quite a few records. Um, in Denmark and over in Paris and England, the people were very nice. I remember I went to Denmark for one night and I stayed there five nights. And oh my God, in Paris, you know how they are. They just love music. The English people are very sweet too. You had a very great success in England, didn't you? Yes, I did. Uh, but I, I didn't, I didn't think that I had this, I, I think the success were wonderful for my first time there. I had around 5,000 people. But I, I'm so used to having tremendous crowd in America that I, I thought that Albert Hall should have been packed to 10,000. And the producer, uh, of the, uh, rather the sponsor of the program told me that he thought it was fine for first, making my first appearance in England, you know, to get 5,000 people. Of course, Paris at the L'Isle Playa, I think that's the right name, but it was packed out two nights straight. The right name, but it was packed out two nights straight. And they were very wonderful. And then I went all through the different, uh, uh, towns in France.
Well, you spent some time there in France. Oh yeah, I stayed there six weeks.

And in Europe, six weeks. So are you going back there? Well, I am, uh, I'm now doing local television work and I want to, uh, uh, it seems that I'm just on the verge to get this coast to coast television job. And, um, of course, if I get that, I won't go back to Europe. But if I don't get it, I think I'll even go to Europe again, around, uh, October maybe. I hope for Europe's sake that you will. Oh, I love to go over there. The people are so nice. Now, where would you go if you were to go to Europe? Well, I know I'd, I know I'd have to go back to the places that I first went to. Uh, I had to go back to Denmark. Oh my goodness. I had about, uh, oh, I think I had around 8,000 people there. Um, uh, but, um, it was 4,000 at this, I don't forget the name of the place, but that one, one night was 4,000. And then the, the other than that, the, the church sees around 2,000 called the Holy Ghost Baptist Church. And that church was about 2,000 years old. I, I really was amazed to, to be able to sing in, uh, uh, uh, a church where people, 2,000 years ago, uh, came in and worshiped God. Oh, that was so wonderful to me. I could never get that church out of my mind. Because I never. So you must go back there? Oh, it was just to stand there one more time. That's beautiful. Where else would you go? Oh, I would, when I go back to, uh, uh, to Europe, uh, next time, I'm going to make it my business to just stay there maybe about six months. I just want to, I want to see all the historical things over there. That's the old world, you know. And it's so much different than ours. Everything of them means so much. It, it, it, it, every building over there has, is dedicated to something great that somebody before you have done to make this a great world. You know, it has, it has taught our new world over here, the, the, the, the, the beautiful way of, uh, of, uh, life. And every time you look at one of those buildings, it, you know, somebody great has been there. And you just, you, you, you look like you, you're back into, to history.
